Sam (FinLedger POC): Hey folks — during the POC ramp today we started seeing intermittent 503/504s when the demo hits ~250 concurrent requests. Started at 10:15 PT.
Aj Patel: Thanks Sam. Can you drop a sample request id + approximate time? Also is this against hosted or the dedicated pool?
Sam (FinLedger POC): hosted in us-west-2. Sample request id: req_20260321_101532_47. I pasted the failing response body below.
Sam (FinLedger POC): ```json
{"error":"backend_unavailable","code":503,"retry_after":null,"trace":"trace-7a9f"}
```
Maria Chen: Ack. First thought: either burstpool exhausted or autoscaler hasn't provisioned extra nodes in time. Do you see high queueing? Can someone pull req_queue_time_ms and burstpool_active tokens?
Tomas Novak: Pulling metrics now. Quick note: we saw autoscale warmup delays yesterday with the new instance boot script — overprovision_delay was 18s. If many small bursts come in, routing may prefer fallback to cheaper variant which can 503 under load.
Kevin Liu: I can check the autoscaler events. infra-bot, show autoscaler events for pool=hosted-usw2-poc since 2026-03-21T10:10:00Z
infra-bot: ```
[10:12:03] scale_decision: want=5 current=3
[10:12:06] provisioning:start instance_id=i-0a1
[10:12:24] provisioning:ready instance_id=i-0a1
[10:12:30] scale_decision: want=8 current=5
[10:12:33] provisioning:start instance_id=i-0b2
[10:12:54] provisioning:timeout instance_id=i-0b2 (boot script hung)
```
Aj Patel: Looks like a provisioning timeout — that explains the lag. Sam, did you configure any aggressive per-route priority or a strict token/window quota?
Sam (FinLedger POC): We did set route-level burst_limit=200 and concurrency_limit=250 for the demo route.
Maria Chen: That concurrency_limit + burst_limit means when the autoscaler lags, the frontdoor may drop into a short-lived 503 to protect downstream. Two mitigation paths: 1) lower the concurrency_limit so we surface backpressure earlier and route to canary variant, or 2) increase preprovision_count or bump burstpool size.
Tomas Novak: Also recommend enabling fallback_policy=variant:nearest-compatible so requests route to a slightly smaller model when capacity is constrained rather than 503.
Kevin Liu: I pushed a temporary change: increased preprovision_count from 2 -> 5 for that pool and extended bootstrap timeout to 90s. Monitoring now.
infra-bot: ```
action: update_pool preprovision_count=5 pool=hosted-usw2-poc
ack: success
```
Sam (FinLedger POC): confirming no 503s in last 3 minutes, demo looks stable. Thank you!
Aj Patel: Great. Follow-ups: we should add a note to the POC checklist to avoid high concurrency_limits without preprovisioning, and include these autoscaler metrics in our runbook. I'll create a short doc.
Maria Chen: Also we should map the customer-visible error -> our internal remediation triggers: if provisioning:timeout seen twice in 10m, escalate to oncall and auto-bump preprovision_count.
Tomas Novak: Agreed. One more ask: can we capture the client-side latencies and KV-cache hit ratios for that route? If latency spikes before 503, it hints at queueing.
Kevin Liu: Pulling traces now, will paste a snippet if we see persistent queue_time > 200ms.
Sam (FinLedger POC): Really appreciate the quick swarm. Two asks from customer: 1) clear guidance for POC sizing, 2) can pricing notes be included if they need larger preprovision?
Aj Patel: We'll send a POC sizing doc + an addendum on reserved capacity pricing for short-term ramps.
Maria Chen: I'll draft the routing/fallback recommendation and drop it in the customer doc.
Kevin Liu: Closing loop — infra-bot, mark incident for monitoring rule: provisioning:timeout frequency >=2 in 10m -> pager oncall
infra-bot: rule created id=rule-7841
Sam (FinLedger POC): Thanks team :thumbsup:
Aj Patel: Nice teamwork :fire:
